items.title: Price pressures persisted in October
items.snippet: Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics ; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios Inflation remained hot in October, according to data from the Labor Department released on Tuesday. Why it matters: The Consumer Price Index shows that even as gasoline prices steadied, inflation pressures elsewhere remained stubborn. By the numbers: CPI rose 0.4% last month, slowing from the 0.6% increase in September. Gasoline prices gained 1% in October, a sharp slowdown from the 9.1% surge in September, the Labor Department said. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, advanced 0.3% for the third straight month, with higher prices for recreation, medical care, car insurance and airline fares contributing to the increase. Of note: The Labor Department did not publish year-over-year inflation rates for October. Last year's government shutdown left a gap in the data that prevents direct comparisons with October 2025. But if one assumes the October 2025 readings were halfway between September and November, year-over-year inflation comes to 4% — or 2.8% excluding food and energy. If everything goes according to plan, the market should give its answer when the company debuts on the Nasdaq exchange next week. Anthropic has set a tentative pricing range of between $1.25 trillion and $1.4 trillion, but several investors we spoke to expect it to price above that range. items.title: Jensen Huang's implosion at Nvidia leaves trail of collateral damage
items.snippet: Jensen Huang's self-destruction has left a trail of collateral damage that threatens to ensnare the board of Nvidia and the AI boom itself . Why it matters: Huang was a singular leader in the global economy, capable of exciting or calming markets with a single sentence and viewed as a virtually indestructible force behind Nvidia's rise. The big picture: His sudden exit after reports of multiple affairs — one with a suspected Chinese spy and the other with a direct report — has wiped out more than $600 billion in value from Nvidia's market cap. "His visionary leadership is going to be missed — it's not going to be replaced," Joel Shulman, CEO of ERShares, which has owned Nvidia shares since 2005, tells Axios. Zoom in: With the uncertainty over Huang's tenure at Nvidia now resolved, the attention will quickly pivot to a slew of unanswered questions, including: What will the investigations uncover? Just because he's gone doesn't mean this is over. items.snippet: Hi HN, the main idea around MergeMax is that the user can look themselves up and compare themselves against all the other people on the board. No sign-in required. We currently support monthly and daily leaderboards. I built MergeMax since I kept seeing people post on X about @poteto's merge count and I knew I could probably create something to easily see her and other popular dev's GitHub public PRs. I quickly found out however that her PRs aren't visible via our methods, since most of her PRs are private/not on GitHub. I also wanted to create a place where people can easily see the amount of merges top accounts do each month, now that agents have the ability to create thousands of PRs themselves. Currently we only support public PRs as well as the contribution total that gets provided by GitHub directly: - A public PR only counts if it's public, merged, and authored by the account that's being looked up, and merged within the specified period. - I use GitHub's search API for PR counts. items.title: Inside the aftermath of the Logan Circle shooting
items.snippet: It took just minutes for a gunman to shoot six people and upend one of D.C.'s busiest neighborhoods. The big picture: Thursday morning's violence left one person dead in a Logan Circle gym and five others injured nearby. The gunman later shot himself, police said. The massive police response shut down streets, sent nearly a dozen schools into lockdown and forced residents to shelter in place. By evening, the streets around VIDA Fitness, where the shooting began, were quiet. Several nearby businesses remained closed, with police tape blocking off storefronts and officers standing watch. Councilmember Brooke Pinto held a vigil . People left flowers and notes outside of the VIDA . "Logan Circle is still a place for love," read one. "VIDA, you are and will continue to be a safe haven for many," read another. But life also carried on: A delivery van unloaded Christmas trees at Whole Foods, and 14th Street bars put out signs advertising happy hour.
